messages:
amal: Dropping a new take on p95 visibility in the heatmap. Two small ideas: 1) micro control inside the left legend for quick toggles (icon + tiny label), 2) a floating mini-toolbar that appears when the chart is focused. Prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/heatmap-visibility
tess: Love the floating toolbar for keyboard users. It solves discoverability without crowding the legend. Does it persist when focus moves to other panels?
amal: Plan is ephemeral: appears when chart or legend receives focus/hover, dismisses on blur. Persistent preference still lives in Settings.
jonah: If it's ephemeral, we should show a subtle affordance in the legend (a faint dot or chevron) so mouse users notice there's more on focus.
rui: Accessibility: toolbar buttons must be reachable by Tab and have visible focus. Also tooltips should be exposed via aria-describedby, not CSS-only hover.
amal: Noted. For copy on the toolbar I mocked: [p95 toggle] label "p95" (tooltip "Show p95 latency line"), [samples] label "Sampling" (tooltip shows current rate). Thoughts on labels?
tess: Keep toolbar labels terse. For sampling use an icon + tiny text "1 in 250" instead of the word Sampling. Tooltip can explain what it means and link to sampling settings.
jonah: UX risk: showing raw rates like "1 in 250" could alarm customers. Proposal: show both rate and an estimate: "1 in 250 (~12k/mo)" in tooltip, but keep toolbar compact.
rui: A11y nit: any item that toggles telemetry must be explicit in copy: "Sends anonymized latency data" somewhere in the tooltip. Also if customers have telemetry disabled org-wide, controls should be disabled with explainer text.
amal: Good point. I'll include disabled state + reason in tooltip if backend reports org-disable flag.
tess: Interaction nit: when the user toggles p95 on, the p95 line should fade in rather than pop to avoid visual jank. Use reduced-motion preference to respect motion settings.
jonah: Also consider a toggle in the context menu (right-click) on the chart for power users. That could include shortcuts for "Show p95" and "Adjust sampling".
rui: Keyboard shortcuts should be discoverable. Add a small "Keyboard: K" hint in the toolbar when opened, and include it in global shortcuts modal. Ensure we document defaults and allow remapping.
amal: Implementation detail: the floating toolbar will be absolutely positioned but anchored via CSS vars to avoid layout shifts. We'll provide an API hook so devs can attach analytics events: event names like "ui.heatmap.p95.toggle" and "ui.heatmap.sampling.open".
tess: Copy tweak: change tooltip copy from "Sends anonymized latency data" to "Sends anonymized latency samples (no request bodies)." Slightly more explicit.
jonah: Visual spec: toolbar uses surface-elev-3 token, 8px round corners, 8px padding, 12px icon size. On dark heatmaps use 16% backdrop to increase contrast. Check against 4.5:1 contrast for icons/text.
rui: Focus management: when toolbar opens via keyboard, first focus lands on first actionable item. On dismiss return focus to original chart element. If modal opens for sampling, trap focus inside modal.
amal: Next steps: I'll update figma with floating toolbar states, disabled state, and motion specs. Tess, can you write the brief for shortcut discoverability? Jonah, can you prototype the fade animation with reduced-motion handling? Rui, can you check wording for tooltip accessibility and the disabled-state copy?
access-bot: Accessibility checklist added to thread: keyboard nav, focus order, aria-describedby usage, reduced-motion respect, contrast verification.
